Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

be involved verb

take part

also take part, get involved, participate, involvement, involve someone, keep out of it, engage in, participation

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.6.1: omnibus negōtiīs nōn interfuit sōlum, sed praefuit
Cic. Att. 14.22.2: cōnsiliīs (Lewis & Short)

intersum, interesse, interfuī

verb, irregular (inter + sum), with the dative

take part in, be present at

With the dative of what one takes part in, or in and the ablative.

Other words

  • particeps esse — have a part in, share in

    adjective particeps, participis, with esse and the genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 9.10.5: hujus igitur bellī ego particeps et socius et adjūtor esse cōgor

  • admisceō, admiscēre, admiscuī, admixtum — draw in, involve; (with sē) get mixed up in

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Haut. 975: Nē tē admisce; Cic. Q. Fr. 3.1.3 (Lewis & Short)

    Of drawing someone into an affair, or meddling in it.

  • implicō, implicāre, implicāvī (implicuī), implicātum (implicitum) — entangle, involve

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.40: contrahendīs negōtiīs implicārī (Lewis & Short)

    Mostly passive: to be caught up in business, a war, mistakes.

Examples

  • quī nōn sōlum interfuit iīs rēbus, sed etiam praefuit

    who was not only involved in these matters but in charge of themCic. Fam. 1.8.1

  • Ita tū istaec tua miscētō nē mē admisceās.

    Stir up those affairs of yours, then, without involving me.Ter. Haut. 783

  • Nē tē admisce: nēmō accūsat, Syre, tē

    Keep out of it: nobody is accusing you, SyrusTer. Haut. 975

See also involve, in charge.
